content.thinking: I need to find the 503 error reference, which appears as "{Gbf7d.1}" in the source. I'll also swap "third-party" for "external" to keep the wording consistent.

action_items.item: Make the account page tolerate an io-pay failure. Put a short timeout and a circuit breaker on the provider client, and render the page without card details when the lookup fails.

Alert on the rate of error responses from io-pay in the payment provider client, and add a synthetic probe of the provider, so a provider outage is flagged separately and sooner than the aggregate io-shop error rate.

Write a runbook and a prepared control, such as a flag that hides the card section, for external provider outages. Include contacting io-pay and checking its status page, so Argus or the on-call engineer has a mitigation to apply.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, starting at {began}. The service was still failing at the last minute of metrics read.

The account page requests were failing with PaymentProviderFailed, raised in the payment provider client when io-pay returned an error for the shopper card lookup. These errors began in the same minute as the onset and peaked during the outage.
A failed io-pay call failed the whole account page request. The page depends on the card lookup while it renders, and the error is raised from the provider client with no fallback or degraded page.

io-pay itself began failing at {began}. Nothing on io-shop's side changed beforehand: there were no production changes and no flag changes. The replicas were all running as before, so the fault lay in the external dependency.
The record does not say why io-pay failed, because it is an external provider and no evidence from its side was available. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: The account page has no degraded mode. When the card lookup fails, the whole page fails instead of rendering without the card details.
Argus has no mitigation for an external dependency failure. It refused to act and could only propose a code change, so the outage continued while the incident was escalated.
Detection relied on the aggregate error-rate alert, which was raised at {alert_raised}, after the onset at {began}. Nothing watched io-pay's error rate directly.

input.executive_summary: From {began}, most requests for shoppers' account pages on io-shop failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service had not recovered by the last minute of metrics read, so the outage lasted at least {duration}, and that is a lower bound. The cause was the external payment provider io-pay returning errors. The account page needs io-pay to render and had no fallback. No deploy, release or flag change preceded the onset. Argus has no safe automated action for an external provider outage, so it opened a draft pull request and escalated to a human, who must review it (AI-1). Argus held the incident for {held}. That measures the response, not the outage.

went_well: Argus picked up the alert within seconds, read metrics, logs, changes and flag history, and identified an upstream dependency failure as the leading candidate with no internal change to blame.
Argus did not take a mitigation that would not have helped, and it escalated with a draft pull request open.
went_wrong: The service was still broken when the incident was escalated. Nothing Argus could do answered this kind of failure.
The leading candidate was never tried or confirmed, and the record has no evidence from io-pay's side.
The account page fails completely when one dependency fails.

input.root_cause: The io-shop account page calls the external payment provider (io-pay) synchronously, and from {began} io-pay returned {Gbf7d.1} for the shopper card lookup. io-shop had no fallback for that failure, so the provider's errors became account page errors. The record does not show why io-pay failed.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for most shoppers
